text:
marcus (prod): OK team — putting a short checklist here for the pilot -> GA acceptance conversation. Hoping we can confirm owners and any non-negotiable blockers by EOD. TL;DR: SLA targets, pricing floor, docs & runbooks, monitoring alerts, rollback/backstop.

jana (eng): Thanks. Can you paste the specific SLA numbers you're asking us to commit to for GA?

marcus (prod): Proposed: 99.9% availability for Hosted API, p50 latency <= 120ms for gen small models, p95 <= 400ms, and a documented compensation policy (credits) for breaches. For Dedicated: 99.95 and an SLO-based support window. Open to feedback.

sophia (solutions): From pilots: two customers asked for a 99.99 option (enterprise) and an explicit data residency clause. We'll need legal/infra signoff.

jana (eng): 99.9/99.95 are probably fine. 99.99 needs dedicated SLA automation and infra capacity commitments — raises capacity/cost planning. Are we gating GA on having 99.99 as a sellable SKU or can we ship GA with it as an enterprise bolt-on?

marcus (prod): Good question. Proposal: GA ships with 99.9/99.95 tiers. 99.99 as an enterprise add-on (marketing + legal caveat). Must document differences clearly.

olivia (support): Staffing note: For GA we need a defined escalation flow and on-call rotation for 24x7 critical incidents. Can we commit to 2-week overlap ramp for the first month of GA so support can shadow ops?

jana (eng): Ops team can do a 2-week overlap; need list of runbooks. Automation for alert triage should be ready — I'll flag the playbooks we still need.

nina (docs): Deadlines: I need final runbooks and API SLA language by Wed next week to ship docs and the pricing page. If any changes after that it's a patch release. Can owners drop PR links here when ready.

liam (sales): Important: pricing floor. We need a simple headline price for hosted gen/embeddings for the public page and a negotiable enterprise band. Also need a one-pager comparing tiers (what's included: caching, priority routing, dedicated capacity).

marcus (prod): Action items so far: (1) jana — confirm infra cost delta for 99.99 SKU and whether auto-fallbacks to cheaper variants are supported (due 48h). (2) olivia — propose on-call overlap schedule and 1-page escalation flow (due 48h). (3) nina — draft SLA language and runbook templates (due 5 business). (4) liam/sophia — compile pilot customer asks that require contract exceptions (due 48h).

jana (eng): Quick technical note — we need to decide on fallback policy for model variants when capacity is constrained. Two options: a) automatic routing to a quantized variant with a quality notice, b) reject with clear error and status code. For production apps, (a) reduces errors but impacts quality. Which do we prefer?

sophia (solutions): Customers prefer (a) as long as we expose the variant in billing and the response includes a header: X-Model-Variant: redwood-gptq-8bit, and a quality flag in JSON. We should also provide a toggle per-customer.

marcus (prod): I support (a) with per-customer toggle + visible header + billing clarity. Add to runbook: how to notify product owners when fallbacks are used >1% of the time over 24h.

olivia (support): Also need a canned customer communication template for degraded-quality fallbacks. I'll draft that and share.

deploy-bot: deploy started for staging: runtime/service-release v2.14.3 by jana — ETA 10m

jana (eng): FYI — the rollback plan for the GA cut: tag vGA-1, automated canary 5% for 4 hours, if error rate > 1% revert to previous model. I will add the specific helm annotations to the runbook.

marcus (prod): Two more items: pricing edge-cases — metered vs committed capacity billing when autoscaling bursts happen; we need a sentence of how bursts are billed and what triggers committed top-ups. And legal needs a template for SLA credits calculation.

liam (sales): For bursts — recommend: committed plan covers baseline throughput; bursts billed per-second at on-demand rate; we should cap burst invoice exposure with a configurable burst cap per account to avoid sticker-shock. Also need a billing FAQ line.

nina (docs): I'll draft the pricing FAQ lines and a short example calc (showing baseline + burst). Please add any sample numbers you want shown.

marcus (prod): OK — summarizing blockers: final SLA/legal wording, runbooks + alerts, support on-call overlap, infra capacity for 99.99 (if we want to sell it at GA), clear fallback policy & per-customer toggles, pricing burst behavior + cap. If any owner can't meet the deadlines above flag now.

jana (eng): I'm on the infra 48h item. If legal or finance slow us on 99.99 we can still ship GA without it.

sophia (solutions): I'll consolidate pilot asks and add the per-customer toggle request.

olivia (support): Drafting escalation and customer comms now, will drop link here in ~24h.

nina (docs): I'll open the docs PR tomorrow and tag reviewers.

marcus (prod): Great — final ask: mark any item you think should block GA (hard blocker) vs must-have-but-not-blocker. I'll collect and propose a go/no-go on Friday. :thumbsup:
